title: Minimum Moves to Balance Circular Array
summary: Given a circular array balance of length n with each element representing the net balance of a person, determine the minimum number of moves needed for all balances to be non-negative.
statement: Given a circular array balance of length n with each element representing the net balance of a person, determine the minimum number of moves needed for all balances to be non-negative. A move consists of transferring exactly 1 unit of balance to an adjacent neighbor. If achieving this is impossible, return -1. Ensure at most one index starts with a negative balance.
constraints: balance has up to 100,000 integers and at most one is negative.
One move transfers one unit to a circular neighbor.
Return the minimum moves to make every balance nonnegative, or -1 when total balance is negative.
hints: Only the single negative position needs incoming units.
Each available unit has a circular distance to that position; closer units should move first.
Sort positive sources by distance and consume until the deficit is filled.
Exchanging a farther chosen unit for a nearer available unit never increases feasibility and strictly lowers cost.
editorial: Exchanging a farther chosen unit for a nearer available unit never increases feasibility and strictly lowers cost.

tests.explanation: The negative position takes one nearby unit and three units across one circular edge, costing four moves.
Four adjacent units and one unit two edges away cost six moves total.
